name: jQuery
summary: The library that normalised the DOM across browsers, now largely superseded by the platform.
what_it_is: A library providing concise DOM selection, traversal, manipulation, events and AJAX with a chainable API, originally papering over deep inconsistencies between browsers.
why_it_matters: jQuery won so completely that the platform absorbed it: querySelectorAll, classList, fetch and addEventListener cover most of what people reached for it to do. It still runs on an enormous share of the web, so you will encounter it — but it belongs here as history and as a diagnostic. Code reaching for jQuery in a new project is usually reaching for habits rather than capability.
suitable_for: Maintaining existing codebases that already depend on it
Legacy environments with genuinely old browser requirements
not_suitable_for: Anywhere bundle size matters — modern DOM APIs cover the same ground for free
verifiable_facts: Still maintained and documented; the API reference is current.
editorial_interpretation: That most of its uses are now covered by native DOM APIs.
context_dependent_guidance: Suitable: Maintaining existing codebases that already depend on it
Suitable: Legacy environments with genuinely old browser requirements
Unsuitable: New projects of any kind
Unsuitable: Anywhere bundle size matters — modern DOM APIs cover the same ground for free
evidence_gaps: No evidence for how much of the web still depends on it, which the "legacy" call implicitly leans on.
wrong_if: A reviewer judges "legacy" too strong for a project still actively maintained, and prefers "declining".
